intro.title: Build resilient checkout state recovery flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a resilient checkout state recovery flow for an e-commerce application. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API to save and restore the user's checkout data, such as cart items and form inputs, so their progress isn't lost if they accidentally close the page or refresh. The core programming concept is managing application state persistence, which involves reading from and writing to localStorage. You will work with JavaScript objects, JSON methods for serialization, and event handlers to implement this recovery feature. By the end, you'll have a checkout page that automatically recovers the user's state, making the shopping experience more reliable and user-friendly.
intro.usecase: This checkout state recovery pattern is essential in e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, where users frequently navigate away from checkout pages. When customers accidentally close tabs, refresh pages, or switch devices, resilient state recovery ensures their cart items, shipping selections, and payment details are preserved. Developers implement this to prevent abandoned carts and provide seamless user experiences across banking apps, travel booking sites, and subscription services. Without this recovery mechanism, users would need to restart complex checkout processes, leading directly to lost revenue and frustrated customers.
